GenerateMoveStateMachine.rationale: CORRECTION to SHARED-FINDINGS section 0, which lists nibbit among the eight hand-rolled ports 'whose C# model builds a BRANCH state, so the equivalence claim is about a distribution'. Nibbit.cs:74 builds a ConditionalBranchState, not a RandomBranchState: it draws nothing (ConditionalBranchState.cs:44-54 ignores its Rng) and returns the first arm whose predicate holds, so the claim is an ordinary deterministic chain and no distribution argument is needed. Graph: INIT_MOVE (a conditional, the initial state) -> BUTT_MOVE if IsAlone, else HISS_MOVE if !IsFront, else SLICE_MOVE; then the fixed cycle BUTT -> SLICE -> HISS -> BUTT (Nibbit.cs:84-86). The port resolves the conditional once in __init__ and carries the same three edges. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py chain`, all THREE encounter configurations alone/front/back, 20 turns): sequences identical and 0 MonsterAi draws on both sides.

guards.what: The conditional is evaluated exactly ONCE per combat and its predicates are constant
guards.rationale: Nibbit.cs:77-82's lambdas read `((Nibbit)Creature.Monster).IsAlone/.IsFront`, which are set by the encounter before combat and never written again (executed: `grep -rn 'IsFront\|IsAlone' src/` resolves every write to NibbitsNormal.cs:24 and NibbitsWeak.cs:22). Nothing points back at INIT_MOVE and it is not re-entered, so resolving it in the constructor is not a shortcut that could drift. NOTE the guarded structure: the `_isAlone` C# `if` (Nibbit.cs:75) chooses WHICH arms are added at all, so the alone build has a single arm and can never fall through to the ConditionalBranchState throw.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit has a real 5-wide range, so a top-end off-by-one would be silently observable as HP 46 never occurring. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [42,46], observed [42,46], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 46 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
